title: Reading the Chart, One Line at a Time

patient.name: Mdm Chua Bee Choo
patient.presenting_complaint: New patient — referred for general eye check-up, occasional blurred distance vision

history.hpc: Mdm Chua has noticed that road signs and bus numbers appear blurry from a distance over the past year. She does not own a pair of glasses. She has come to SNEC for the first time, referred by her GP after a community vision screening flagged reduced vision. She is to undergo Modified LogMAR distance visual acuity testing as part of her initial work-up before seeing the doctor.
history.pmhx: No previous eye surgery. No known ocular disease. Type 2 diabetes diagnosed 3 years ago, on medication.
history.family_hx: Father had cataract surgery in his 70s
history.social_hx: Works at a hawker stall. Does not currently wear any glasses.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Early nuclear sclerosis bilaterally, otherwise unremarkable
examination_findings.fundus: To be assessed by doctor — query diabetic retinopathy screening required

modified_logmar_va.right_unaided: 6/12, plus 1 letter on the 6/9 line (recorded as 6/12 +1)
modified_logmar_va.method: Modified LogMAR (M&S System), tested at calibrated working distance, right eye first, occluder used and wiped with alcohol before and after
modified_logmar_va.result: Vision improves with pinhole in both eyes, suggesting refractive error as the main cause of reduced vision

investigations.near_va: Not tested today — distance VA only as ordered

diagnosis: Modified LogMAR distance visual acuity testing completed for both eyes. Vision is reduced unaided (6/12 right, 6/18 left) but improves significantly with pinhole, suggesting an uncorrected refractive error is the predominant cause. For doctor's review, including diabetic eye screening given her history of diabetes.

immediate: Perform hand hygiene and wipe the occluder with alcohol wipes before starting
Position patient comfortably facing the Modified LogMAR chart at the calibrated working distance (check the displayed working distance on screen)
Confirm patient is not wearing any glasses or contact lenses (none owned)
Test the right eye first by convention, occluding the left eye
Ask patient to read all 5 letters/numbers on each line from left to right, starting from the top (largest) line, proceeding down until she cannot read all 5 letters on a line
Document the last line on which all 5 letters were read correctly, noting any extra correct letters on the next line as +1, +2, etc.
Repeat the same process for the left eye, occluding the right eye
Since both eyes read 6/12 or worse, apply the pinhole occluder and repeat the test for each eye to assess for improvement
Wipe the occluder with alcohol wipes again and perform hand hygiene after the test
Document all results (unaided and pinhole) clearly for both eyes and pass to doctor
follow_up: Doctor to perform refraction to confirm spectacle prescription
Doctor to assess for diabetic retinopathy given her history of diabetes — fundus examination/dilated retinal photo may be ordered
Patient to be scheduled for spectacle dispensing if refraction confirms need
patient_education: Explain that the chart test helps find out how clearly she can see at a distance
Explain that the pinhole result suggests glasses may significantly improve her vision
Advise patient on the importance of regular diabetic eye screening, even without visual symptoms

key_points: Confirms patient identity and confirms whether patient wears any glasses or contact lenses
Explains the Modified LogMAR chart procedure clearly to a first-time patient
Notes relevant medical history (diabetes) that may affect overall eye assessment
Performs hand hygiene and wipes occluder with alcohol wipes before starting
Tests the right eye first by convention, with the other eye correctly occluded
Requires patient to read ALL 5 letters on a line before proceeding to the next line down, stopping at the first line not fully read
Documents the last completed line correctly, including any +1/+2/+3/+4 extra letters read on the next line
Applies pinhole correctly since vision is 6/12 or worse, and documents the pinhole result for each eye
Recognises that improvement with pinhole indicates a refractive cause for reduced vision
Understands VA testing is a baseline measurement and does not replace formal refraction
Does not prescribe glasses independently — refers to doctor for refraction
Identifies the need for diabetic eye screening given the patient's history
Documents unaided and pinhole VA results accurately for both eyes using correct notation
Wipes occluder with alcohol wipes before and after testing (infection control)
Hands results to doctor and flags diabetic history for retinal screening
Provides clear explanation to the patient about the purpose and result of the test
